questions.question: Q: Explain Blumler and Katz's Uses and Gratifications theory.

points.text: Uses and Gratifications theory argues that audiences actively use media to fulfil four needs: information/education (learning about the world), entertainment (enjoyment and escapism), social interaction (connecting with others through shared media), and personal identity (finding role models and reinforcing values).

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between an active and a passive audience?

points.text: A passive audience absorbs media messages without question, as suggested by the hypodermic needle model. An active audience selectively engages with media, interpreting and using content to fulfil personal needs. Modern audience theory generally views audiences as more active than passive.

questions.question: Q: How do media producers target audiences?

points.text: Producers use demographic data (age, gender, income) and psychographic profiles (values, interests, lifestyle) to identify target audiences. They then design content, marketing, and distribution to reach them — e.g. a teen horror film is marketed on TikTok and Snapchat, not in broadsheet newspapers.

questions.question: Q: Evaluate the view that audiences are more active than passive in the digital age.

points.text: Digital technology has made audiences more active: social media enables interaction, prosumers create content, and streaming gives choice over what to watch and when. However, algorithms curate content, creating filter bubbles that limit genuine choice. Audiences may be active within constrained options, and the illusion of choice may mask continuing media influence.

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: Media producers use detailed audience profiling to target and appeal to specific groups. Demographic and psychographic data inform decisions about content, scheduling, and marketing. For the 'This Girl Can' campaign, the BBC targeted women who were put off exercise by conventional fitness marketing. The psychographic profile was women who valued health and wellbeing but felt excluded by idealised fitness imagery. The campaign used realistic body types and empowering language to appeal to this audience, distributing content via social media platforms where the target audience was active. The use of social media as a distribution channel was significant — the target audience of 14-40 year old women are heavy social media users. The shareable, emotionally resonant content encouraged peer-to-peer distribution, extending reach beyond paid advertising. However, targeting has limitations. The campaign's focus on 'real' bodies may have alienated some women who felt judged for being fit and conventionally attractive. Hall's reception theory reminds us that audiences can negotiate or oppose the preferred reading. Streaming platforms demonstrate increasingly sophisticated targeting. Netflix uses viewing data to commission and recommend content tailored to specific audience segments, creating niche products that traditional broadcasters would not produce.
